source: README.md §0.4 'Detail action row — always visible': 'Export brief (primary, ink) · Share · ☆ Watch · ＋ Tag, all four on the detail header, 8px gap, padding:8px 14px; radius 6, secondary = white with rgba(0,0,0,.25) border and #F5F2EE hover'; operator rulings 3.1 (remove the Immediate ▾ dropdown) and 3.2 (the action-row + Tag is the only trigger)
notes: The dc.html #sys 'Actions · stat block' block (Export brief / Share / ☆ Watch example) carries the identical padding:8px 14px;border-radius:6px;font-size:12.5px values as a worked example of the same button chrome; README's own 8px gap / padding:8px 14px; radius 6 prose is used as the primary source line for this spec, per the harness convention of preferring the exact-numbers statement over the illustrative artboard block.

This mount's `watch` slot is a plain ActionButton placeholder (variant=secondary), not the real WatchButton (out of this spec's reach: WatchButton owns its own persistence and is audited separately if a lane adds a spec for it) — sufficient to measure the ROW's own gap and the three buttons this component itself owns (Export, Share, + Tag).

children.name: Export brief (primary)
children.note: README: primary, ink fill, padding 8px 14px, radius 6.

children.name: + Tag (dashed pill)
children.note: ActionRow.tsx: dashed variant, 1px dashed rgba(0,0,0,.25). Operator 3.2: this is the ONLY + Tag trigger a detail surface should render outside the tag row itself (the tag row's own trigger is audited separately — both existing is correct per 3.2's own text: 'Applied workspace tags still render as a row under the title; that row displays tags, it does not carry the trigger' — meaning the TAG ROW's trigger is the violation to look for, not this one).

forbid.name: an 'Immediate ▾' band-change dropdown in the action row
forbid.reason: Operator 3.1: 'Remove the Immediate ▾ dropdown from the regulation detail action row... Action row is exactly Export brief (primary) · Share · ☆ Watch · + Tag.' ActionRow.tsx itself never renders this control (it lived in HeroPriorityDropdown, a separate component some detail surfaces compose alongside ActionRow) — a MATCH here confirms the shared part is clean; the forbid check on the composed page (page-frame.json) is what catches a surface that still renders HeroPriorityDropdown next to it.
